title: Exported parseDuration now returns seconds instead of milliseconds, silently changing the value every existing caller receives by 1000x
rationale: This is an exported function whose return unit changed: a caller that previously received 2000 for "2s" now receives 2, and "1500ms" now yields the fractional 1.5 rather than an integer. Any caller that feeds the returned value to a millisecond-based API (timeouts, expiry math) is off by a factor of 1000; the change is only safe if every caller is updated in the same commit, which cannot be verified from this diff.

title: Guard does not reject negative limits, which SQLite treats as unbounded
rationale: In SQLite a negative LIMIT means no upper bound, so fetch_orders(conn, 0, -1) returns every row in the table — exactly the outcome the new docstring claims the guard prevents. A caller passing a computed limit that goes negative (or -1 as an 'all rows' sentinel) silently bypasses the check.

title: Remaining() silently changes its return unit from bytes to whole megabytes
rationale: The exported method previously returned bytes; it now returns whole megabytes while keeping the unit-less name Remaining, so every existing caller receives a value 2^20 times smaller than before with nothing at the call site signalling the change. A caller still treating the result as bytes — for example gating an upload against a byte count — will misbehave; a separate RemainingMB accessor or a unit-bearing name would preserve the old contract for existing callers.

title: Guard does not reject negative limits, which SQLite treats as unbounded
rationale: In SQLite a negative LIMIT means no upper bound on rows returned, so fetch_orders(conn, 0, -1) pulls the entire orders table into memory — exactly the outcome the new guard and docstring claim to prevent. The check enforces only the upper bound and needs a lower bound too.

title: Lookup no longer returns the documented ErrNotFound sentinel, breaking callers that match it
rationale: ErrNotFound is exported with the documented contract that Lookup returns it when no user has the id, so callers match it with errors.Is or == to handle missing users gracefully. Replacing it with a bare fmt.Errorf breaks that match, so every not-found lookup is now indistinguishable from an unexpected error and takes the caller's generic error path. Wrapping the sentinel preserves both the id in the message and the sentinel contract.

title: Lookup no longer returns the sentinel ErrNotFound
rationale: Callers matching on errors.Is(err, ErrNotFound) — the documented contract of the exported sentinel on line 8 — now never match, so any not-found handling keyed to that sentinel silently stops working. Wrap with %w instead of replacing the error.

title: Lookup no longer returns the documented ErrNotFound sentinel
rationale: Lookup returns a fresh fmt.Errorf value that does not wrap ErrNotFound, so errors.Is(err, ErrNotFound) is always false for callers. Existing callers branching on not-found, e.g. to create a default user, silently take the wrong path.

title: Remaining() silently changes unit from bytes to megabytes
rationale: Remaining() now returns megabytes where it previously returned bytes, while the name and int64 type give no indication of the unit change. Any caller comparing the result to a byte threshold would silently over-admit by 2^20; the shown diff does not include the callers, so the consequence rests on the assumption that at least one such caller exists outside the dashboard.

title: Remaining changes from bytes to megabytes under an unchanged, unit-less name in a byte-denominated API
rationale: New and Record deal in bytes while Remaining now returns megabytes under the same unit-less name, so any caller pairing Remaining() with byte values — its behavior before this change — is off by a factor of 2^20. If the dashboard is the only caller, a separate megabyte accessor or a rename keeps the byte-level contract intact.

title: Exported parseDuration now returns seconds instead of milliseconds, a silent 1000× contract change
rationale: The return value changes by 1000× for every input ("2s" now yields 2 instead of 2000, "1500ms" yields 1.5 instead of 1500), and ms inputs now produce fractional values where all previous returns were integers. No caller updates appear in the diff, so unless every caller was audited and adjusted, any caller feeding this into a millisecond-based API silently receives a value 1000× smaller. Because the function is exported, the affected callers may extend beyond this repository.

title: Negative limit bypasses the MAX_PAGE guard and returns the whole table
rationale: The guard only rejects limits above MAX_PAGE, but SQLite treats a negative LIMIT as unbounded, so fetch_orders(conn, 0, -1) still loads every order into memory — the exact outcome the check and docstring promise to prevent. Since limit is untrusted, a negative value is a plausible input.

title: Negative limit bypasses the MAX_PAGE guard and returns the whole table
rationale: SQLite treats a negative LIMIT as unbounded, so fetch_orders(conn, offset, -1) returns every row in the table — exactly the full-table pull the new docstring says cannot happen. The guard needs to reject limit < 0 as well as limit > MAX_PAGE.

title: Remaining() changes its return unit from bytes to megabytes for all callers
rationale: New and Record are byte-based, so Remaining() returning whole megabytes leaves the type's API mixed-unit. The concrete breakage — an existing caller comparing the result against byte quantities and getting a value 2^20 times smaller — rests on callers not shown in the diff; any such caller silently miscomputes.

title: Lookup no longer returns ErrNotFound, breaking documented contract
rationale: The package documents ErrNotFound as the value returned by Lookup, and any caller using errors.Is(err, ErrNotFound) now gets false, since the wrapped-identity contract is replaced by an ad-hoc fmt.Errorf with no %w. Callers that branch on ErrNotFound silently fall through to the error path.
